summary: Peter Zieme worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (1960–1965), he served at the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (1965–2007) and the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1992–2007).

Peter van der Veer worked in religious studies, Indology, and Sinology, studying at the University of Groningen and Utrecht University. His posts include the University of Amsterdam (1992) and director of the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity (~2008–2021).

Peter von Bohlen studied at Halle, Berlin, and Bonn, learning under Franz Bopp, Georg Freytag, and August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He spent his career at the University of Königsberg, becoming ordinary professor of oriental literature in 1828 and 1830.

Peter von Bradke was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Leo Meyer and Rudolf von Roth at Tartu and Tübingen, before earning degrees at Jena and Giessen. He served as an extraordinary professor at the University of Giessen from 1886 to 1896.

Peter von Köppen was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the National University of Kharkiv (~1810–1814) and the University of Tübingen (~1819–1821), and held a post at the Ministry of State Property.

Petra Kieffer-Pülz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. A pupil of Heinz Bechert, she held posts at the University of Göttingen (attested 1995), the Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur Mainz (~2000), and served as Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society (~2005).

Petra Maurer works in Tibetology and Indology, having studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She has held posts at the University of Munich, the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Phakchok Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at the Dzongsar Institute (~1995–2003) and under several traditional teachers, including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. He serves as Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling.
Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

Phanit Jetjiravat specializes in Buddhist studies and earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where they were advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn was a historian and sinologist who studied at Harvard and Georgetown. He served on the faculty at the University of Chicago (1963–1978) and later as a professor of history and East Asian languages at Harvard University from 1978.

Philip A. Mellor works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester in 1989 and later served as Professor of Religion and Social Theory and Head of the School of Humanities at the University of Leeds.

Philip Boas Yampolsky worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University and under Yoshitaka Iriya, later serving as an adjunct associate professor and East Asian Library librarian at Columbia (1968–1996) and chair at the Numata Center (1991–1996).

Philip Clart is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied under Daniel L. Overmyer from ~1990 to 1997. In ~2008, he became Professor of Chinese Culture and History at the University of Leipzig.
Philip Deslippe works in religious studies and Indology. He has been a graduate student (attested 2020–2026) and a teaching associate (attested 2020) at the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Philip Kapleau was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, Soen Nakagawa, and Sogaku Harada. He founded the Rochester Zen Center and the Chapin Mill Retreat Center (1996).

Philip L. Quinn worked in philosophy and religious studies, earning degrees from Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He taught at Brown University (~1970–1985), became the John A. O'Brien Professor of Philosophy at Notre Dame in 1985, and presided over the APA (1994–1995).

Philip Lutgendorf is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Chicago (~1967–1987). He joined the University of Iowa faculty in 1985 and served as president of the American Institute of Indian Studies from 2010 to 2018.

Philip Novak works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Notre Dame (~1968–1972) and Syracuse University (~1975–1981), and taught at Dominican University of California from ~1980 to 2017.

Philip Whalen was active in Buddhist and religious studies. After earning a BA at Reed College (~1946–1951), he studied under Richard Baker (1972) and held posts at Dharma Sangha (1984), South Ridge Zendo (~1984–1987), and Hartford Street Zen Center (1991).
